title: Surjectivity on global sections of an affine extension with quasi-coherent ends
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be its affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Then $\Gamma(X,g):\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_2)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_3)$ is surjective.

source.place: Schemes, Tag 01IE, lemma-extension-quasi-coherent, proof from Pick m to its end

proof.text: Map the given short exact sequence to its underlying abelian sheaves. The forgetful functor is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits, so ShortExact.map_of_exact applies. Lean uses the proved source preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf and the finite-limit instance of Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Limits. No quasi-coherence of the middle term is required.

The quasi-coherent kernel has exact positive-degree standard affine Cech complexes by lem-pc-affine-cech-complex. The proved source cechAcyclicOnAffines_of_isQuasicoherent packages this property. Every cover of an affine open has a finite standard refinement, proved by exists_basicOpen_cover_of_isAffineOpen in the same source module. Apply the topological Cech section-lifting criterion through its proved wrapper surjective_app_of_cechAcyclicOnAffines to the affine open top of Spec R.

The carrier and function of moduleSpecGammaFunctor.map S.g are definitionally the global sections and their map. ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective converts the obtained surjectivity to Epi. The quotient quasi-coherence hypothesis is retained unchanged but is not needed. The zero ring gives the empty spectrum, included in the sheaf lifting theorem.

proof_origin.place: G3 reuse of proved cechAcyclicOnAffines_of_isQuasicoherent and surjective_app_of_cechAcyclicOnAffines with exact module forgetting; underlying lifting proof is Stacks Tag 01EU.
